established_prior_art_core: Controlled glycosylation of glucose with defined long-chain fatty alcohols can yield alkyl glucosides / alkyl polyglucosides.
Glycerol and propylene glycol are hydrophilic polyols, not long hydrophobic tails.
Glycosylglycerol and propylene-glycol glucoside chemistry have prior art.
A glycerol- or glycol-based architecture becomes a candidate surfactant only when a defined hydrophobic domain is present.
disclosed_subject_matter.open_research_claim: A precisely defined petroleum-derived hydrophobic building block, optionally linked through glycerol or propylene glycol and combined with a glucose-derived hydrophilic domain, may yield a reproducible amphiphile with a distinct structure or useful property profile not anticipated by known APG and glycol-glucoside prior art.
negative_controls_and_falsification: Crude oil plus aqueous glucose is not presumed to synthesize a surfactant.
Physical mixing is not covalent synthesis.
Matched mass alone is not confirmed structure.
Viscosity or cosolvent effects from glycerol/propylene glycol are not proof of a new amphiphile.
An exact prior-art match defeats novelty.
Failure of independent replication defeats the result claim.
claim_ladder: LEVEL_4 interfacial function confirmed against controls
LEVEL_7 novelty supported by prior-art review
